articles.title: USC Star JuJu Watkins Completes Recovery from ACL Injury
articles.summary: USC star JuJu Watkins is set to return to action after completing her lengthy recovery from an ACL injury that occurred in March 2025.
articles.content: USC star JuJu Watkins has finally completed her lengthy road to recovery from an ACL injury and is set to return to action for the Trojans. Watkins' absence was deeply felt last season as USC struggled without its top player, finishing with an underwhelming record. The 2026-27 season is a new chapter for the team, with high expectations as they enter the campaign as the No.3-ranked team in the country and are expected to contend for a national championship. Watkins' return has significantly boosted the Trojans' chances of achieving this goal, given her status as arguably the best player in college basketball when healthy. Watkins' ACL tear occurred during a pivotal moment in the NCAA Tournament, as she was going for a layup against Mississippi State when she collided with multiple defenders. The impact was immediate and severe, causing Watkins to crumple to the ground and clutch her right knee in pain. She required assistance off the court as she struggled to put weight on her injured leg. This devastating injury forced Watkins to undergo surgery just weeks later, effectively ruling out any possibility of returning for the remainder of the 2025 season. The lengthy recovery period has now spanned nearly two years, with Watkins set to take the floor again when USC opens its new campaign. As Watkins continued her rehabilitation journey, she had to adopt a more deliberate approach than usual. She revealed that her rehab process involved slowing down and revisiting the fundamental skills of basketball, which she hadn't done since learning them initially. This meant spending time in the weight room before progressing to stationary movements like catching and shooting hoops. According to Watkins, this gradual progression was essential for her recovery, despite feeling the urge to rush back onto the court sooner. The lengthy rehabilitation period allowed Watkins to appreciate the journey and its challenges. She described it as a humbling experience that taught her patience and made her stronger in the long run. JuJu Watkins' recovery from an ACL injury has been a long and challenging process for the USC star. She suffered the injury on March 24, 2025, during a game against Mississippi State in the NCAA tournament, where she played just five minutes before leaving due to her injury. Her performance was impressive despite the short time she spent on the court, as she managed to collect three points before exiting the game. This setback came after an impressive run of durability for Watkins, who had played 37 games across her first two collegiate seasons. The impact of her absence was felt by USC, which struggled to a 18-14 record and lost in the second round of the NCAA tournament as a No. 9 seed. Despite these challenges, Watkins' experience has likely made her stronger and more patient, a sentiment she's shared about her recovery process. articles.title: Federico Garcia Lorca's Play La Bola Negra Adapted into Film
articles.summary: The critically-acclaimed film La Bola Negra is based on an unfinished play by Federico Garcia Lorca that was written in 1936.
articles.content: La Bola Negra, a critically-acclaimed film released this year, has its roots in an unfinished play penned by Spanish poet and playwright Federico Garcia Lorca in 1936. The play shares its name with the movie, which translates to "the black ball" in English. This unusual origin story is not uncommon for works created by LGBTQ+ artists from over a century ago. Some of these pioneering creatives faced significant challenges getting their work published or recognized during their lifetimes. James Baldwin's novel Giovanni's Room, for example, was almost destroyed when his agent advised him to burn the manuscript. Emily Dickinson's romantic poetry, which some critics believe was dedicated to her sister-in-law Susan Gilbert Dickinson, remained undiscovered until after her passing. Federico Garcia Lorca's play La Bola Negra is a rare exception in that it has been adapted into a film. The movie has garnered significant critical acclaim this year, making its historical origins all the more remarkable. As the story unfolds, the focus shifts to a wealthy young man's attempt to gain entry into an exclusive casino in Granada, a pivotal moment that sets the stage for the narrative's exploration of social hierarchy and acceptance. The members of this elite group use a voting system to decide who gains admittance, with a white ball signifying approval and a black ball indicating rejection. This decision-making process serves as a microcosm for the societal pressures and expectations faced by the characters in Lorca's play. Meanwhile, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi bring their unique vision to the story, reimagining Lorca's incomplete work as a testament to the enduring power of art and creativity. By interweaving three distinct time periods, 1932, 1937, and 2017, the directors craft a rich tapestry that celebrates the lives of gay men across a century, all connected by their shared passion for Lorca's writing. The film's co-directors sought to fill a significant gap in queer representation by creating a story that connects their community across generations. To do so, they delved into archives and old letters to piece together the narrative, using their imagination to envision how Lorca might have ended his writing. Their efforts paid off, resulting in a film that not only honors Lorca's work but also explores the complexities of being part of a marginalized community. The directors' approach was akin to detective work, as they scoured through historical documents to uncover the threads that bind their community together. articles.title: Jacksonville Jaguars Enjoy Unbeaten Home Record This Season
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have gone undefeated at home this season and boast a 10-1 record over the past two seasons under coach Liam Coen.
articles.content: The Jacksonville Jaguars are enjoying a remarkable home-field advantage this season, marking a significant turnaround from their recent struggles on their own turf. The team has gone undefeated at EverBank Stadium so far this year and boasts an impressive 10-1 record over the past two seasons under coach Liam Coen. The last time the Jaguars achieved such success at home was during the 2006-07 seasons, when they won more than 10 home games in a two-year span under then-coach Jack Del Rio. The current team is now on track to potentially break this record with victories in their final three home games against Tennessee, Pittsburgh, and Washington. The Jaguars' dominance at EverBank Stadium has been evident in recent weeks, as they have barely been challenged at home. Their wins over Cleveland, New England, and Indianapolis have been particularly impressive, with the team outscoring its opponents by a significant margin of 271-75 in their last seven regular-season games at "The Bank". The team's recent performance at home has caught many off guard, but coach Liam Coen's coaching and the team's overall chemistry seem to be key factors in their success. With three more home games remaining on their schedule, the Jaguars are well-positioned to continue their winning streak and make a strong push for the playoffs. The Jaguars' winning streak is a welcome respite from years of struggling on their home turf. This season's success has been built on strong performances at EverBank Stadium, where the team has managed to turn around their fortunes despite limited capacity due to renovations. The $1.4 billion renovation has reduced seating capacity to 42,500 this season and 60,000 last year, yet the Jaguars have found a way to thrive in these conditions. Their home-field advantage is not due to any major factors like large stadiums or noise-advantageous domes, but rather seems to be driven by supply-and-demand dynamics that favor die-hard season-ticket holders. The team's appreciation for their limited opportunities at EverBank Stadium has been evident in their determination to make the most of them. The Jaguars' offense is firing on all cylinders, evident in their dominant performance against the Colts. They capitalized on their opportunities, scoring touchdowns on three of their first five possessions and building a significant 28-0 lead by halftime. This impressive start has given the team a substantial lead that will be difficult for the Colts to overcome. The Jaguars' ability to convert on third down is also worth noting, with a success rate of 6 out of 12 against Indy. This brings their season total to 48.2%, ranking them third in the league behind Cincinnati and San Francisco. The team's success on the field has come at a cost, however, with the loss of DaVon Hamilton to a season-ending injury. As a result, Jacksonville may be in the market for a nose tackle to fill this void, with potential options including Jordan Davis and Moro Ojomo from Philadelphia, as well as Grover Stewart from Indianapolis. Rookie standout Bhayshul Tuten continues to impress, breaking his career high with 104 yards rushing and adding two catches for 55 yards and a score. His 39-yard touchdown run in the first half was particularly notable, showcasing his speed and agility. The Jaguars' Parker Washington had a relatively quiet game on Sunday, failing to score in consecutive games for the first time this season. He managed just one catch for 16 yards and was targeted twice, a slight departure from his usual performance. In other news, the Jaguars opted to mix up their punt-return duties, using Travis Hunter and rookie Josh Cameron alongside Washington. This decision came as the team seeks to improve its average punt return of 3.5 yards, which currently ranks them 31st in the league. The game was played with several key players missing from the starting lineup, including safety Eric Murray, defensive end Travon Walker, right guard Ezra Cleveland, and safety Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have now played on Thursday Night Football for the 15th time, holding a record of 6-8 in these midweek matchups. articles.title: Federal Judge Dismisses Complaint Against Former FBI Agents
articles.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a complaint against two former FBI agents accused of lying to Congress about their involvement in an investigation into President Joe Biden's son Hunter.
articles.content: A federal judge has dismissed a criminal complaint against two former FBI agents accused of lying to Congress about their involvement in an investigation into President Joe Biden's son Hunter. The case centered on testimony given by Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides before the House Judiciary Committee in 2023, where they allegedly misled lawmakers about their roles on the Foreign Influence Task Force and their work on the FBI's Hunter Biden investigations. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui ruled that the government had failed to establish probable cause that the agents had intentionally lied to Congress. A prosecutor in the case had privately acknowledged that the criminal complaint was flawed during a telephone call last week, according to the magistrate judge's ruling. This admission raises questions about the strength of the government's case against the former FBI agents. The attorney leading the prosecution is Jeanine Pirro, a former Republican Hill staffer who has been involved in high-profile cases in the past, including a failed indictment of six sitting members of Congress over a social media video criticized by President Donald Trump. Despite the judge's ruling, it remains possible for the case to proceed if federal grand jurors are convinced of probable cause. However, given Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui's finding that the complaint did not meet the legal standard, it seems unlikely that the Justice Department will be able to convince the grand jurors. This outcome is further complicated by the judge's previous criticism of the government for attempting to bring additional charges without proper authorization. The dismissal of the case against ex-FBI agents Floris and Benavides has sparked a mixed reaction from Trump allies. Both men had been involved in investigating security issues related to the 2020 presidential election, which Trump has repeatedly claimed was rigged. Their defense team has issued a statement defending their clients' integrity, calling them "patriots" and "public servants" who are innocent of any wrongdoing. The team also expressed concern that the government may try to charge the case again in secret, behind closed doors, where they would be unable to present their side of the story. articles.title: OpenAI's Lobbyist Warns 2028 Candidates on AI Governance
articles.summary: Chris Lehane advises prospective presidential candidates that artificial intelligence will be a defining issue in the next election and they need more than just talking points to address it.
articles.content: OpenAI's top lobbyist is advising prospective 2028 candidates on the importance of having a governing philosophy for artificial intelligence in their campaigns. According to a memo obtained by some contenders, Chris Lehane argues that AI will be a defining issue in the next presidential election and that candidates need more than just talking points about key issues. Lehane specifically warns Democrats that opposing infrastructure needed to build the technology could put them on the wrong side of the debate. He also cautions that local projects such as data centers can have far-reaching consequences, implying that a fight over these facilities is not just about local politics but has broader implications for the country's technological development. The memo represents an effort by OpenAI to shape how presidential hopefuls think and talk about AI, suggesting that the company sees this technology as a key area of influence in the upcoming election. The memo, sent to a select group of individuals, outlines OpenAI's vision for how presidential hopefuls should approach discussions around artificial intelligence in the 2028 election. According to insiders, the company is aiming to shape the conversation around AI and its implications on various aspects of society, including affordability, tax codes, child protection, and technological superiority. The memo emphasizes the need for candidates to demonstrate their ability to maintain human oversight over critical decisions made by AI systems. OpenAI's efforts suggest that the company believes AI will play a significant role in the 2028 election, with its capabilities continuing to advance and public awareness increasing. The implications of America's leadership in AI are far-reaching, according to a recent report. A world where the US takes the lead will be vastly different from one dominated by the Chinese Communist Party. This stark contrast highlights the importance of addressing the role of artificial intelligence in shaping the country's future. As the midterm elections approach, both parties will face increasing pressure to outline their stance on AI. The "shadow primary" is already underway, with each party's eventual standard-bearer set to play a crucial role in determining the tone for their respective approaches. This development underscores the urgent need for clear policy direction on this critical issue. The candidates who ultimately succeed will not rely solely on promises of technological salvation or ignore the challenges posed by AI altogether. Instead, they will need to articulate a nuanced and forward-thinking vision for harnessing the power of artificial intelligence while mitigating its risks. Journalists from various news outlets are being invited by OpenAI to participate in a program that focuses on explaining artificial intelligence to the public. The initiative aims to equip these journalists with the necessary knowledge and tools to effectively communicate AI-related concepts and developments. The program's goal is not only to educate but also to help shape the global conversation around AI, encouraging participants to develop nuanced and forward-thinking ideas about harnessing its potential while mitigating its risks. articles.title: Career Change at 61: Former Travel Industry Professional Becomes Flight Attendant
articles.summary: A 61-year-old man has retrained as a flight attendant after decades in the travel industry, finding that his skills are well-suited to the role.
articles.content: Richard Woulfe marked his 60th birthday with a sense of restlessness and discontent with his life's trajectory so far. He had been in the travel industry for decades, but felt an insatiable urge to pursue something new. Woulfe's dissatisfaction led him to retrain as a flight attendant at the age of 61, embarking on a third chapter in his life. He is now employed by a major US airline and has found that his skills as a flight attendant are well-suited to his personality. He believes that qualities commonly associated with Gen X individuals, such as flexibility and a willingness to listen, have been invaluable assets in his new role. Woulfe's decision to change careers was motivated by a desire for challenge and personal growth. The pandemic had a significant impact on Woulfe's business, causing his main markets to shut down due to travel restrictions imposed by countries like Thailand. As a result, he was forced to return to Chicago and take some time off, where he spent quality time with his parents. Woulfe's father was struggling with health issues at the age of 90, and Woulfe wanted to be there for him as much as possible during this challenging period. This experience likely had a profound impact on Woulfe, who would soon find himself re-evaluating his life and career choices. After celebrating his 60th birthday in March 2023, Woulfe's mother noticed that he seemed restless and asked if everything was okay. Woulfe reassured her that he wasn't depressed but rather feeling unfulfilled, which sparked a conversation about his future plans. Woulfe reached out to a friend who had been working as a flight attendant since 2018 for advice on how to get back into the workforce. His friend's encouragement was timely, and Woulfe began to consider making a career change that would bring him new challenges and opportunities for personal growth. As Woulfe reflected on his life, he realized he wasn't ready to retire at 60. He considered making a change that would bring new challenges and opportunities for growth. The transport industry had long fascinated him, dating back to his childhood when he was more interested in the journey than the destination. Woulfe's friend, who had been working as a flight attendant since 2018, offered valuable advice on this potential career path. He encouraged Woulfe to leverage his experience in travel and hospitality for a new role. With that encouragement, Woulfe began exploring the possibility of becoming a flight attendant himself. He discovered that several major US airlines were hiring thousands of flight attendants at the time. This sparked his interest further, and he started applying to various carriers. Although there was some back-and-forth due to personal circumstances, Woulfe eventually secured an interview within 72 hours. As he prepared for this new career, Woulfe noticed a trend among his peers - many Gen-X individuals were willing to acquire new skills and pursue non-traditional careers at an older age. He found this particularly inspiring, especially when he encountered candidates in their 60s and 70s who were also vying for the role of flight attendant. As Richard Woulfe approached his 60th birthday, he realized that retirement wasn't for him. Instead of slowing down, he decided to acquire new skills and stay in the job market. Woulfe's decision paid off as he found a fulfilling career as a flight attendant, where his life experience and ability to listen came into play. His mantra is simple: "I hear you," whenever a passenger raises an issue, showing that people want to feel heard. This approach has been key to his success in this role. The last two years have been amazing for Woulfe as he's had the opportunity to travel to various destinations, from international cities like San José, Costa Rica and Vancouver, to small domestic places like Colombia, South Carolina. His message to anyone considering a lifestyle pivot is clear: if something is calling you, it's worth taking a risk. articles.title: Nasdaq 100 Index Declines Amid Concerns Over Valuing AI Firms
articles.summary: Billionaire investor Howard Marks has expressed doubts over traditional valuation methods for predicting future earnings of AI companies like Anthropic.
articles.content: Billionaire investor Howard Marks has pinpointed a major challenge in valuing AI companies like Anthropic. In an interview on "Bloomberg: The China Show" on Monday, Marks acknowledged that traditional valuation methods often fail when it comes to predicting the future earnings of AI firms. Value investors typically try to estimate a company's earnings five years from now to determine if its current stock price is attractive. However, Marks doubts that this approach can be effectively applied to many AI companies. Anthropic, the developer of the popular chatbot Claude, has filed to go public in what could become one of the largest initial public offerings (IPOs) on record. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 index experienced a significant decline last week, plummeting by approximately 1,400 points or nearly 5% over Thursday and Friday. Despite this drop, the index remains in positive territory for the year, having risen around 13% so far. However, the broader market's performance has been even more impressive, with the Nasdaq 100 soaring by a substantial 160% since the end of 2022. The index has effectively doubled its value over this period, rising from under 11,000 points to just below 28,400 points. Investors are being cautioned against making impulsive decisions in response to short-term market fluctuations, with billionaire Howard Marks emphasizing that there is no reward for "hyperactivity" in the investment business. This approach is in line with the long-term investing philosophy championed by Warren Buffett, who has built a reputation for holding onto stakes in companies like Coca-Cola and American Express since acquiring them in the mid-1990s. Valuing AI companies has proven to be a challenging task due to market trends favoring speculative investments over traditional value-based approaches. Investors like Michael Burry have sounded alarms about potential bubbles in the AI sector, citing aggressive accounting practices, hidden debts, and circular deals as warning signs that are often overlooked by enthusiastic investors.
